mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Annualized CPI inflation exceeding 3.5% signals persistent price pressures that trigger monetary tightening expectations, reducing equity risk appetite and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 3.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous positive employment growth (PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5%) and declining unemployment (UNRATE monthly change < -0.1pp) indicate robust labor market conditions that strengthen corporate earnings momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.1pp (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 growth > 2.5%), rising housing starts (HOUST growth > 1.0%) reflect sustained consumer spending strength that drives positive equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 2.5% and HOUST growth > 1.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production index above 100 (INDPRO > 100) indicates robust manufacturing output, which correlates with improved corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO > 100 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that triggers inflation concerns and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate increases (FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25pp) and accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 3.0%) signal aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 3.0%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 3.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In recessionary regimes (GDPC1 growth < -0.5% and UNRATE > 4.5%), declining housing starts (HOUST decline > 0.5%) indicate deteriorating consumer demand that drives negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < -0.5% and UNRATE > 4.5% and HOUST decline > 0.5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 growth < -0.5% and UNRATE > 4.5% and HOUST decline > 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
